newsitem.title: USA: Hate crimes up in Chicago, murder and rape down.
newsitem.headline: Hate crimes up in Chicago, murder and rape down.

text.p: There were more hate crimes and arson fires in Chicago in the first six months of the year, but murders, rapes and robberies fell, according to police statistics.
The number of reported hate crimes rose 31 percent to 127 over the first six months of 1996.
Chicago Police Department spokesman Paul Jenkins said the rise was almost entirely in white-on-black and black-on-white crime.
But he added that the March beating of a 13-year-old black youth allegedly by three white teenagers caused a surge.
"One thing about hate crimes is we can point to incidents that cause an increase in the number of those to be reported," Jenkins said, citing the March beating.
Arson rose nearly 16 percent to 834 fires in the first six months of the year compared with the first half of 1996.
The number of rapes fell by 10.5 percent to 1,250 and murders dropped 9.6 percent to 346.
